name: Activity
grades: A: no errors and at most 1 warning. B: no errors. C: 1 error. D: 2 errors. F: 3 or more. Each rule counts once, however many places it fires. Hints never count.

1.name: Main control in the bottom third

2.name: Close X or back arrow at the top

4.name: Full-bleed color, dark or art background

7.name: Stop or finish control named with a verb

9.name: Panel, sheet or alert layered at the bottom

v1.name: Lesson or quiz step
expect: A progress mark and one question or instruction line near the top
An answer area of tiles, bubbles or a keypad right under the question
A close X or back arrow at the top and one main button in the bottom third

v2.name: Timer or live tool
expect: A full-bleed color or dark background that takes over the screen
One big readout, such as a timer, a ring or a percent
One main control low on the screen

v4.name: Trip or order map
v4.lead: Trip or order on a map
expect: A status readout, a stop or cancel control, or a sheet layered over the map
No answer tiles: the task is a status, not a question

not_checked: What happens after the tap: whether the answer turns green, the timer runs or the sheet slides up needs a second state.
Whether the progress mark moves, the readout ticks or the game animates: one screenshot has no motion.

rules.says: A bottom button or link is faint against its fill and easy to miss.
rules.why: Faint grey buttons at the bottom are easy to miss: Continue on Uxcel Go and Cancel on Uber Eats. Seen on 10 of 50 checked screens.

rules.says: The instruction is small and pale beside the artwork.
rules.why: The instruction is small and pale next to the artwork. Seen on 5 of 50 checked screens.

rules.says: Dense small type or tiny numbers crowd the screen while the person is busy.
rules.why: Dense small type or tiny numbers sit in the screen while the person is busy with a task. Seen on 4 of 50 checked screens.

rules.says: No close X or back arrow to leave the task.
rules.why: 31 of 50 checked screens have "Close X or back arrow at the top".

rules.says: No progress mark or live readout shows where the person is.
rules.why: 37 of 50 checked screens have "Progress or live readout".

rules.says: No question or instruction line says what to do.
rules.why: 36 of 50 checked screens have "One question or instruction line".

rules.says: No main control in the bottom third.
rules.why: 30 of 50 checked screens have "Main control in the bottom third".

rules.says: The main control sits above the bottom third.
rules.why: Of the 30 screens that have "Main control in the bottom third", 28 put it in the bottom third.

rules.says: The close X or back arrow is not at the top.
rules.why: Of the 31 screens that have "Close X or back arrow at the top", 30 put it in the top third.

rules.says: The panel or sheet is not layered at the bottom.
rules.why: Of the 12 screens that have "Panel, sheet or alert layered at the bottom", 10 put it in the bottom third.

rules.says: More than one main control competes in the bottom third.
rules.why: Of the 30 screens that have "Main control in the bottom third", 27 show exactly one.

rules.says: More than one close X or back arrow sits on the screen.
rules.why: Of the 31 screens that have "Close X or back arrow at the top", 30 show exactly one.

rules.says: More than one question or instruction line competes for attention.
rules.why: Of the 36 screens that have "One question or instruction line", 34 show exactly one.

rules.says: More than one stop or finish control is on the screen.
rules.why: Of the 16 screens that have "Stop or finish control named with a verb", 16 show exactly one.

rules.says: More than one panel or sheet is layered at the bottom.
rules.why: Of the 12 screens that have "Panel, sheet or alert layered at the bottom", 12 show exactly one.

rules.says: A lesson or quiz step with no answer area under the question.
rules.why: 11 of 13 Lesson or quiz step screens have "Answer area under the question".

rules.says: Lesson or quiz step screens are not checked for "Panel, sheet or alert layered at the bottom".
rules.why: Only 3 of 13 Lesson or quiz step screens have it, so position/9 does not apply to a screen of this variant.

rules.says: The timer or live tool does not take over the screen with a full-bleed color or dark background.
rules.why: 13 of 14 Timer or live tool screens have "Full-bleed color, dark or art background".

rules.says: Timer or live tool screens are not checked for "Panel, sheet or alert layered at the bottom".
rules.why: Only 0 of 14 Timer or live tool screens have it, so position/9 does not apply to a screen of this variant.

rules.says: A trip or order screen with no map behind the task.
rules.why: 9 of 9 Trip or order map screens have "Map behind the task".

rules.says: Text or a close control is too faint against what is behind it.
rules.why: Accessibility guidelines ask for 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text: 18 pt, or 14 pt bold (button labels are bold). Controls, such as a close or back glyph, need 3:1. Below 3:1 is an error; from 3:1 to 4.5:1 on smaller text it is a warning. Checked on the labels of buttons, the lines of the parts marked as key text, and the close and back glyphs. Not checked on a dimmed screen or over a photo or a pattern, or on the label of a greyed-out button (the guidelines leave out controls that cannot be used yet). Faint placeholder text in an empty field is only a hint, since iOS's own placeholder grey is about 1.7:1.

rules.says: Text is smaller than 11 pt.
rules.why: Apple lists 11 pt as the smallest text size on iOS. Measured from the height of each line, so it is about right, not exact. Checked on the parts marked as key text.

rules.says: A control sits under the status bar or the home indicator.
rules.why: The status bar row at the top and the bottom 34 pt, where the home indicator sits, belong to the system on phones without a home button. Flagged when a control reaches the status bar row or comes within 17 pt of the bottom edge, so a button that only touches the area is not counted.

rules.says: A close or back control is drawn smaller than 13 pt.
rules.why: Apple asks for a 44 x 44 pt tap area. The standard close X in a bar is drawn about 13 to 17 pt across inside that area, so only a smaller drawing is flagged. A screenshot cannot show the tap area itself, so this is a hint.
